newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajikistan says opposition violated truce deal.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan says opposition violated truce deal.

text.p: Tajikistan protested to the United Nations on Thursday, accusing Islamic guerrillas of violating a provisional truce signed on Wednesday in northern Afghanistan, a spokesman for the Tajik president said.

"There was shooting in the town of Garm this morning when the opposition attacked our battalion," spokesman Zafar Saidov told Reuters. "We are going to issue a note of protest to the U.N. special representative in Tajikistan, Gerd Merren."
Russia's Itar-Tass news agency quoted a Tajik foreign ministry statement as saying that if the opposition continued its attacks the government would have to respond.
Tass said Merren had informed opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri about Tajik President Imamali Rakhmonov's protest.
It was not clear whether the opposition admitted fresh fighting or how Nuri had reacted to Rakhmonov's protest.
Rakhmonov and Nuri agreed on a ceasefire from midnight on Wednesday during their peace talks in northern Afghanistan.
Forces loyal to Rakhmonov defeated their opponents in a civil war in 1992 and forced them to flee to Afghanistan.
The truce deal was struck after a string of clashes between troops and rebels, in which the latter gained ground in eastern and central Tajikistan after years of cross-border war.
The provisional truce was due to last at least until another meeting between Rakhmonov and Nuri in Moscow on December 19.

Russia's Interfax news agency quoted Tajik officials as saying that two government soldiers in Garm, 150 km (100 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe, had been killed and another three wounded during the rebel attack on Thursday.
The rebels are besieging the government battalion in Garm.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said that fighting also raged on Thursday in Komsomolabad region, 120 km (80 miles) northeast of Dushanbe, where police checkpoint had been attacked by some opposition fighters. This report could not be confirmed.
A senior aide to president Boris Yeltsin, Yuri Baturin, who is now in Dushanbe arranging the Moscow Rakhmonov-Nuri meeting, said that separate violations of the truce cannot be ruled out.
"There is no guarantee that this agreement is automatically carried out," Tass quoted Baturin as saying. Baturin said that he thought the truce had a good chance of surviving.
In a separate development two bombs rocked the centre of Dushanbe on Thursday, killing one person and injuring another.
"The blasts were caused by two explosive devices," Interior Minister Khumdin Sharipov told Reuters by telephone, adding that he had no information about who planted them.

A corpse lay near Dushanbe's main post office where the first explosion went off shortly after midday (0700 GMT). Bystanders said an injured person had been taken to hospital after the blast which smashed windows in nearby buildings.
The second bomb near the Pakistan embassy wrecked a Lada car. The buildings were quickly sealed off by police.
Nerves in the Tajik capital are on edge following a spate of attacks against Russian servicemen who help prop up Rakhmonov's shaky administration.
The recent attacks have been widely blamed on opposition guerrillas, but the opposition has not claimed responsibility.
"The opposition had no hand in this," Yusuf Khakimov, an opposition representative based Dushanbe, said after Thursday's explosions. "It is not in our interests."
